# Resolve the whole OH plugin graph and its API generation

## Platform difference

An unchanged package name does not imply an unchanged Dart API or an OH implementation in the resolved dependency graph.

## Implementation

PiliPlus switches share/orientation forks and adjusts callers to older APIs. Kazumi changes connectivity result handling, playback completion and PopScope alongside plugin sources. ConnSSH changes picker APIs and later repairs code_text_field selection. Enjoy Plus moves toast/preferences into overrides; its unpinned declarations rely on lockfile revisions. Xingmu pins a video-player fork behind a controller abstraction. MR fixes a missing monorepo subdirectory in CI-generated overrides. KikoFlu explicitly pins its native-capable forks.

## Applicability

Resolution must consider app-facing packages, backend packages, Dart constraints and native dependencies. These examples include both older and newer API generations; no single version set fits all projects.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

An override can solve source selection without ensuring semantic compatibility. A dependency local to another developer is not reproducible. A Git URL without a ref can change on a new resolution. Do not confuse package repository name with pubspec name.

## Verification

Inspect resolved package sources and lockfile commits, trace the imported API into its backend, and test the exact methods the application uses on OH and other supported targets.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
